State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Smt. Sarita Panda vs Branch Manager, Life Insurance ... on 21 April, 2023
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
 CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 AFR / NAFR

 CHHATTISGARH STATE
 CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
 PANDRI, RAIPUR

 Date of Institution: 21/02/2019
 Date of Final Hearing: 21/04/2023
 Date of Pronouncement: 21/04/2023
 COMPLAINT CASE No.- CC/2019/09
 IN THE MATTER OF :
 Smt. Sarita Panda
 W/o. Late Kamal Kishor Panda,
 Ward No.34, LIG-25, Housing Board Colony, Kabir Chowk,
 RAIGARH (C.G.)
 Through: Shri Sanjeev Sharma, Advocate
 ... Complainant.
 Vs.
 1. Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India,
 Divisional Office, Magarpara,
 BILASPUR (C.G.).
 2. Zonal Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India,
 Central Zonal Office, Jeeva Shikha, 60-B, Hosangabad Road,
 BHOPAL (M.P.)
 Through: Shri D. Dutta & Shri G.V.K. Rao, Advocates
 ... Opposite Parties

 CORAM: -
 HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAUTAM CHOURDIYA, PRESIDENT
 HON'BLE SHRI GOPAL CHANDRA SHIL, MEMBER
HON'BLE SHRI PRAMOD KUMAR VARMA, MEMBER
 PRESENT: -
None appeared for the complainant even in second round of call.
 Shri D. Dutta & Shri G.V.K. Roa, Advocates for the opposite parties.
O R A L O R DE R
 PER: - JUSTICE GAUTAM CHOURDIYA, PRESIDENT

 This complaint, under
section 17
of the Consumer Protection Act,

 1986 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short) has been filed by the

 complainant feeling aggrieved by repudiation of insurance claim and

 alleging deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties. The

 complainant has sought direction to the opposite party for payment of

 sum assured under the insurance policy Rs.25,00,000/- with interest @

 12% p.a. from the date of filing complaint, compensation for deficiency in

 service committed by the opposite parties Rs.15,00,000/-, compensation
Dismissed Page 1 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 for mental agony Rs.5,00,000/- and cost of litigation along with any other

 relief which this Commission deems fit to award.
2. Brief facts necessary for disposal of this complaint, as per the

 complaint, are that the husband of the complainant Late Kamal Kishor

 Panda obtained an early death claim insurance policy bearing

 No.358922519 and premium of which were being regularly paid. The

 insured Kamal Kishor Panda died during subsistence of the policy on

 05.03.2017 and the complainant is entitled to get the benefits of the

 insurance policy. Complainant has further averred that original bond

 paper of the said insurance policy was misplaced somewhere therefore

 she requested the opposite parties to provide second copy of the same but

 was not provided by them with intention of depriving the complainant

 from the benefit of the policy. Legal notice dated 18.07.2018 was sent to

 the opposite parties, which was replied by the opposite party No.1

 denying their liability of payment of insurance claim. Again a legal notice

 was sent on 26.11.2018 which was not replied. For getting the second copy

 of policy bond the complainant had also moved application under
Right

 to Information Act
, but the document was not provided even after filing

 First Appeal in that matter. Hence, alleging deficiency in service in non-

 payment of sum insured as death benefit of the insured, this complaint is

 filed seeking reliefs as aforesaid in paragraph No.1.
3. The opposite parties in their joint written version have admitted the

 fact of issuance of insurance policy and averred that insurance policy

 under Amulya Jeevan-2 scheme for sum assured Rs.25,00,000/- and

 annual premium of Rs.17,425/- was issued on 15.08.2015 in favour of

 husband of the complainant. The opposite parties have denied the story of

 misplacing of policy bond and stated that in fact the original policy was
Dismissed Page 2 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 deposited in the office of the opposite parties with regard to getting the

 insurance claim. The opposite parties have further averred that as the

 insured died within one year and eight months of commencement of the

 policy hence being a case of early death claim it was investigated as per

 rule and on investigation it revealed that the insured Late Kamal Kishor

 Panda while making proposal for getting insurance cover had given

 incorrect information regarding his health in column No.11 - Personal

 History. Incorrect information was given by him with regard to Column

 No.11 (b) (d) and (e) of the Proposal Form. In fact before giving proposal

 for the insurance, the insured was suffering SOL in right Lung (Space

 Occupying Lesion of Lung) i.e. lung cancer, for which he was treated in

 Apollo Hospital Bilaspur (C.G.). He was also suffering Hydatid Cyst and

 CCAM of Right Lung. The insured was in knowledge of his above

 diseases before giving insurance proposal as he got treatment for the said

 diseases from Apollo Hospital Bilaspur (C.G.) which is evident from

 documents regarding his treatment. As the insurance policy was obtained

 by the insured by deliberately concealing the material facts regarding his

 health, hence as per terms & conditions of the insurance contract the claim

 was repudiated and in doing so no deficiency in service was committed

 by the opposite parties. It is prayed that this complaint be dismissed with

 cost.
4. In support of the complaint the complainant has filed copies of

 legal notice dated 18.07.2018 and its reply dated 27.07.2018. Legal notice

 dated 28.11.2018. Complainant has filed her affidavit in support of the

 complaint and additional affidavit dated 12.01.2020 and affidavit of Dr.

 Prashant Kumar dated 12.01.2020, who was called to visited the home of

 the complainant for treating her husband but after examining husband of
Dismissed Page 3 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 the complainant, Dr. D. Prashant Kumar declared her husband Kamal

 Kishor Panda as dead. He issued a note mentioning probable cause of

 death as Cardio Respiratory Arrest. Whereas the opposite parties have

 filed affidavit of Mr. P. Anand Rao, Manager (Legal), Divisional Office,

 Life Insurance Corporation of India, Bilaspur and copy of insurance

 proposal, insurance policy, claim form, claim investigation report,

 repudiation letter, insured‟s Treatment Documents of AIIMS, New Delhis

 and that of Apollo Hospital, Bilsapur and reply of legal notice.
5. None appeared for the complainant on the date of final arguments

 even after second call, however we have minutely gone though the

 complaint, affidavits and documents filed by the complainant. We have

 heard arguments of learned counsels for the opposite parties and perused

 the affidavit and documents filed by them.
6. In support of the complaint the complainant has filed her affidavit

 and later on filed another affidavit dated 12.01.2020 in which she has

 clarified the facts as per objections raised by the opposite parties in their

 written version. In the said affidavit she has stated that in the copy of

 proposal form filed by the opposite parties the entries made are not

 handwritten by her husband. It appears that signature of her husband was

 obtained on a blank form and later on Agent of the opposite parties has

 filled the proposal form, hence nothing was concealing by her husband.

 She has also stated that the opposite parties before issuing the insurance

 policy got the insured physically examined by Dr. Amit Soni and on

 giving examination report as fit, insurance of her husband was done by

 the opposite parties. She has further stated that her husband died of

 cardio respiratory arrest and this fact is also affirmed by the report of Dr.
Dismissed Page 4 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 D. Prashant Kumar and thus the cause of death of her husband is not

 cancer as alleged by the opposite parties.
7. Learned counsels for the opposite parties have argued that it is not

 in dispute that the insured died within one year and eight months from

 the date of commencement of the policy and being a case of early death

 claim the opposite parties conducted investigation under the provisions of
Section 45
of the Insurance Act 1938 as amended by Insurance Laws

 (Amendment) Act, 2015 which provides for calling in question a policy of

 life insurance at any time within three years from the date of issuance of

 the policy or the date of commencement of risk on the ground of fraud

 like the active concealment of a fact by the insured having knowledge or

 belief of the fact or concealment of facts, omission etc. On such

 investigation it revealed that the insured was a patient of lung cancer and

 took treatment in AIIMS New Delhi and Apollo Hospital Bilaspur.

 Treatment documents received from the said Hospitals have also been

 brought on record As Exhibit NA/OP-6 & NA/OP-7 respectively. These

 facts were concealed by the insured while making proposal for insurance

 policy and in the relevant column of the proposal form, i.e. column No.11

 Personal History he replied all the questions regarding his health,

 treatment taken, hospitalization for more than a week, question that he

 ever suffered or suffering from cancer, diabetes, tuberculosis, High Blood

 pressure Low Blood pressure etc. has replied in „No‟. Especially the

 information given in reply of question at (b), (d) and (e) of the Column

 No.11 are relevant which were given incorrect as evident from the

 treatment record of the AIIMS New Delhi as well as that of Apollo

 Hospital Bilaspur. Hence the claim was repudiated in accordance with the

 terms and conditions of the policy and they have not committed any

 deficiency in service.
Dismissed Page 5 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.
8. We have considered the above arguments as well as the statement

 of the complainant in her affidavit. So far as the contention of the

 complainant regarding the information in the proposal form was not filled

 by her husband and in fact it was filled by Agent of the Insurance

 Corporation is concerned, we do not find any substance in this objection

 looking to the fact that in the proposal form, declarations and wherever it

 was necessary the insured had signed it and the signature is not

 questioned by the complainant. Otherwise also except statement of the

 complainant there is nothing on record which can cogently prove that the

 handwriting is not of the insured himself, nor report of any handwriting

 expert is brought on record.
9. The second contention of the complainant is that her husband died

 of cardio respiratory arrest as opined by the Dr. Prashant Kumar and not

 due to cancer. In this regard we have gone through the report of Dr. D.

 Prashant Kumar, filed as Exhibit A-11 and also the affidavit of Dr. D.

 Prashant Kumar. Dr. D. Prashant Kumar has given his opinion regarding

 cause of death as probable cause and mentioned in his report that "He

 declared the patient dead at 5:00 am, probable cause: Cardio Respiratory

 Arrest". This report shows that it was probable cause of death and there

 is nothing on record to show the definite cause of death. But at the same

 time it is also true the insured was diagnosed as suffering from SoL in

 Right Lung (Space Occupying Lesion of Lung) and Hydatid Cust and

 CCAM of Right Lung at Apollo Hospital Bilaspur and was treated there.

 At the AIIMS New Delhi in February 2016 the insured was present to

 Medical Oncology Department with the history that he was diagnosed as

 soft tissue sarcoma at private hospital Bilaspur in 2012. He received

 multiple line of therapy including 3 lines of chemotherapy radiation
Dismissed Page 6 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 therapy as well as surgical intervention (Lobectomy) at Local Hospital. In

 the AIIMS New Delhi reevaluation of disease was done. Biopsy review

 was suggestive of Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma and CECT

 indicate stable disease. Medicines were prescribed and advised for regular

 follow up. In January 2017 Response assessment was done which showed

 disease progression. Under the head DIAGNOSIS AND STAGE it has

 been mentioned that "STS RT lung operated case (Bilobectomy).
10. The above all the facts and treatment history goes to show that the

 insured was suffering lung cancer he was given chemotherapy, radiation

 therapy as well as surgical intervention Lobectomy but these facts were

 concealed by him while making proposal for insurance. The facts

 concealed were material in nature hence the opposite parties Insurance

 Corporation were having right to repudiate the claim and in doing so they

 have not committed any deficiency in service.
In the regard the principle

 laid down by the Hon‟ble Apext Court in its judgement in the case of
Branch Manager, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Dalbir Kaur
,

 2020 SCC Online SC 848 is squarely applicable. That was a case in which

 from the medical records obtained during the course of the investigation it

 was clearly indicated that the deceased was suffering from a serious

 preexisting medical condition which was not disclosed to the insurer and

 in fact the undergone treatment for such medical condition was in

 proximity to the date of his death and said history was, in spite of specific

 queries, not disclosed in the proposal form. In such a situation it was held

 as material concealment of fact and insurance company was not held

 liable to pay any amount.
The principle
laid down by
the Hon‟ble Apex

 Court in its previous judgement in the case of Satwant Kaur Sandhu Vs.
Dismissed Page 7 of 8
Complaint No.: Smt. Sarita Panda Date of Pronouncement:
CC/19/09 Vs. 21/04/2023
 Branch Manager, Life Insurance Corporation of India & Anr.

 New India Assurance Company Limited, (2009) 8 SCC 316 was also

 discussed in that case wherein it was held that : -
"In a contract of insurance, any fact which would influence the
 mind of a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept or not
 to accept the risk is a "material fact" - If the proposer has
 knowledge of such fact, he is obliged to disclose it to insurer
 particularly while answering questions in the proposal form -
 Any inaccurate answer to said questions will entitle the
 insurer to repudiate its liability under the policy".
11. So far as the contention of the complainant that the proposed

 insured was physically got examined by the opposite parties by Dr. Amit

 Soni and upon his fitness report only the insurance policy was issued, is

 concerned the term used „Physical Examination‟ itself goes to show that

 the proposed insured was only physically examined on the basis of

 history disclosed by him, but when in his personal history he had

 concealed material facts, then the opposite parties cannot be faulted at on

 this ground. Had there been the case that all the correct information

 regarding personal history was given, then the opposite parties would

 have an opportunity to take decision accordingly or to underwrite in

 perspective those facts. But by concealing material facts regarding

 personal history of the proposed insured, the opposite parties were

 deprived of taking appropriate decision as per the actual state of health of

 the proposed insured. Thus, we do not find any substance this contention

 also, of the complainant.
12. Therefore, for the foregoing discussion, we do not find any

 substance in this complaint it accordingly fails and is dismissed. No order

 as to cost.
(Justice Gautam Chourdiya) (Gopal Chandra Shil) (Pramod Kumar Varma)
 President Member Member
